subtype: Approach: asking a teacher for help to talk it out [Revision]
passage: Note from the class teacher. Gargi came to me at the end of Monday, hands twisted together. She had tried to make up with Raghav at the water tank, but within a minute both were shouting again. "We can't fix it alone," she said. "Will you help?" I asked them to come in after school. I sat between them and set one rule: each of us speaks while the others listen. Raghav went first, fast and angry. Then Gargi told her side. By the end Raghav was staring at the floor, and Gargi's shoulders had dropped. They left together, still awkward, but talking.

qa.q: Where did Gargi and Raghav's first attempt end in shouting?
qa.a: Their first attempt ended in shouting at the water tank.

qa.q: What did Gargi realise after the shouting, and how might Gargi have felt?
qa.a: Gargi realised they could not fix it alone; twisted hands suggest Gargi felt worried and a little ashamed of the shouting.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Gargi try if the talk with the teacher still stays tense, and why?
qa.a: Gargi could write down what matters most to say, or wait a few days before trying again with calmer feelings. Both could work because they slow the anger.

qa.q: How might Raghav see the talk with the teacher?
qa.a: Raghav went first and fast, then stared at the floor while Gargi spoke, so Raghav may have felt defensive and then thoughtful once listening.

grounding: Her first attempt to make up ends in shouting, so she notices they cannot fix it alone and asks the class teacher to help them take turns speaking.
